BRUCINE: A poweful vegetable alkaloid, found, associated with strychnine, in the seeds of different species of Strychnos, especially in the Nux vomica. It is less powerful than strychnine. Called also brucia and brucina.
BITARTRATE: A salt of tartaric acid in which the base replaces but half the acid hydrogen; an acid tartrate, as cream of tartar.
BRUSHITE: A white or gray crystalline mineral consisting of the acid phosphate of calcium.
BUSHINESS: The condition or quality of being bushy.
BOYISH: Resembling a boy in a manners or opinions; belonging to a boy; childish; trifling; puerile. A boyish, odd conceit. Baillie.
BDELLIUM: 1. An unidentified substance mentioned in the Bible (Gen. ii. 12, and Num. xi. 7), variously taken to be a gum, a precious stone, or pearls, or perhaps a kind of amber found in Arabia. 2. BACKSHEESH: In Egypt and the Turkish empire, a gratuity; a "tip".
BLUE-BONNET: 1. A broad, flat Scottish cap of blue woolen, or one waring such cap; a Scotchman. 2. (Bot.) A plant. Same as Bluebottle. 3. (Zoöl.) The European blue titmouse (Parus coeruleus); the bluecap.
BOMBOLO: A thin spheroidal glass retort or flask, used in the sublimation of camphor. [Written also bumbelo, and bumbolo.]
BRUCITE: (a) A white, pearly mineral, occurring thin and foliated, like talc, and also fibrous; a native magnesium hydrate. (b) The mineral chondrodite. [R.]
BAVIN: 1. A fagot of brushwood, or other light combustible matter, for kindling fires; refuse of brushwood. [Obs. or Dial. Eng.] 2. Impure limestone. [Prov. Eng.] Wright.
BAY-ANTLER: The second tine of a stag's horn. See under Antler.

BOBBER: One who, or that which, bobs.
BROTHER-IN-LAW: The brother of one's husband or wife; also, the husband of one's sister; sometimes, the husband of one's wife's sister.
BOBWHITE: The common qua(Colinus, or Ortyx, Virginianus); -- so called from its note.
BASSOON: A wind instrument of the double reed kind, furnished with holes, which are stopped by the fingers, and by keys, as in flutes. It forms the natural bass to the oboe, clarinet, etc. Note: Its compass comprehends three octaves. For convenience of carriage it is divided into two parts; whence it is also called a fagot.
BURNISH: To cause to shine; to make smooth and bright; to polish; specifically, to polish by rubbing with something hard and smooth; as, to burnish brass or paper. BICALCARATE: Having two spurs, as the wing or leg of a bird.
BIOGENESIS: (a) A doctrine that the genesis or production of living organisms can take place only through the agency of living germs or parents; -- opposed to abiogenesis. (b) Life development generally.
BOWNE: To make ready; to prepare; to dress. [Obs.] We will all bowne ourselves for the banquet. Sir W. Scott.
BLANKET POLICY: One that covers a group or class of things or properties instead of one or more things mentioned individually, as where a mortgage secures various debts as a group, or subjects a group or class of different pieces of property to one general lien.
BRETHREN: pl. of Brother. Note: This form of the plural is used, for the most part, in solemn address, and in speaking of religious sects or fraternities, or their members.
BIPOLAR: Doubly polar; having two poles; as, a bipolar cell or corpuscle.
BEVILE: A chief broken or opening like a carpenter's bevel. Encyc. Brit.
BOUGHT: 1. A flexure; a bend; a twist; a turn; a coil, as in a rope; as the boughts of a serpent. [Obs.] Spenser. The boughts of the fore legs. Sir T. Browne. 2. The part of a sling that contains the stone. [Obs.] imp. & p. p. of Buy. Purchased; bribed.
BOMB: A container filled with explosive, incendiary, or other destructive material.
BASIFUGAL: Tending or proceeding away from the base; as, a basifugal growth.
BILIN: A name applied to the amorphous or crystalline mass obtained from bile by the action of alcohol and ether. It is composed of a mixture of the sodium salts of the bile acids.
BUG: An insect; a defect in a computer program.

BEAUTIFY: To make or render beautiful; to add beauty to; to adorn; to deck; to grace; to embellish. The arts that beautify and polish life. Burke. Syn. -- To adorn; grace; ornament; deck; decorate. To become beautiful; to advance in beauty. Addison.
BORDELAIS: Of or pertaining to Bordeaux, in France, or to the district around Bordeaux.
BOTTOM FERMENTATION: A slow alcoholic fermentation during which the yeast cells collect at the bottom of the fermenting liquid. It takes place at a temperature of 4º - 10º C. (39º - 50ºF.). It is used in making lager beer and wines of low alcohol content but fine bouquet.
BRANCHIOPODA: An order of Entomostraca; -- so named from the feet of branchiopods having been supposed to perform the function of gills. It includes the fresh-water genera Branchipus, Apus, and Limnadia, and the genus Artemia found in salt lakes. It is also called Phyllopoda. See Phyllopoda, Cladocera. It is sometimes used in a broader sense.
BATTERY: 1. The act of battering or beating. 2. (Law) The unlawful beating of another. It includes every willful, angry and violent, or negligent touching of another's person or clothes, or anything attached to his person or held by him. 3. (Mil.) (a) Any place where cannon or mortars are mounted, for attack or defense. (b) Two or more pieces of artiller...
BROMA: 1. (Med.) Aliment; food. Dunglison. 2. A light form of prepared cocoa (or cacao), or the drink made from it.
BUBBLING JOCK: The male wild turkey, the gobbler; -- so called in allusion to its notes.
BEDSTRAW: 1. Straw put into a bed. Bacon. 2. (Bot.) A genus of slender herbs, usually with square stems, whorled leaves, and small white flowers. Our Lady's bedstraw, which has yellow flowers, is Galium verum. -- White bedstraw is G. mollugo.
BONDER: 1. One who places goods under bond or in a bonded warehouse. 2. (Masonry) A bonding stone or brick; a bondstone. A freeholder on a small scale. [Norway] Emerson.
BALLISTA: An ancient military engine, in the form of a crossbow, used for hurling large missiles.
BECOMINGNESS: The quality of being becoming, appropriate, or fit; congruity; fitness. The becomingness of human nature. Grew.
BACKBITER: One who backbites; a secret calumniator or detractor.
BAILEY: 1. The outer wall of a feudal castle. [Obs.] 2. The space immediately within the outer wall of a castle or fortress. [Obs.] 3. A prison or court of justice; -- used in certain proper names; as, the Old Bailey in London; the New Bailey in Manchester. [Eng.] Oxf. Gloss.
BALNEAL: Of or pertaining to a bath. Howell.
BOMBAZINE: A twilled fabric for dresses, of which the warp is silk, and the weft worsted. Black bombazine has been much used for mourning garments. [Sometimes spelt bombasin, and bombasine.] Tomlinson.
BISON: A humpbacked shaggy-haired wild ox native to North America and Europe.
BEWITCH: 1. To gain an ascendency over by charms or incantations; to affect (esp. to injure) by witchcraft or sorcery. See how I am bewitched; behold, mine arm Is like a blasted sapling withered up. BENDING: The marking of the clothes with stripes or horizontal bands. [Obs.] Chaucer.
BIANNUAL: Occurring twice a year; half-yearly; semiannual.
BRASHY: 1. Resembling, or of the nature of, brash, or broken fragments; broken; crumbly. Our progress was not at all impeded by the few soft, brashy floes that we encountered. F. T. Bullen. 2. Showery; characterized by brashes, or showers.
BELDAM: 1. Grandmother; -- corresponding to belsire. To show the beldam daughters of her daughter. Shak. 2. An old woman in general; especially, an ugly old woman; a hag. Around the beldam all erect they hang. Akenside.
BEVER: A light repast between meals; a lunch. [Obs.] Beau. & Fl. To take a light repast between meals. [Obs.]
BULBUL: The Persian nightingale (Pycnonotus jocosus). The name is also applied to several other Asiatic singing birds, of the family Timaliidæ. The green bulbuls belong to the Chloropsis and allied genera. [Written also buhlbuhl.]
BROMIZE: To prepare or treat with bromine; as, to bromize a silvered plate.
BONNYCLABBER: Coagulated sour milk; loppered milk; curdled milk; -- sometimes called simply clabber. B. Jonson.
BISULPHITE: A salt of sulphurous acid in which the base replaces but half the hydrogen of the acid; an acid sulphite.
BLOOD VESSEL: Any vessel or canal in which blood circulates in an animal, as an artery or vein.
BERGANDER: A European duck (Anas tadorna). See Sheldrake.
BIPONTINE: Relating to books printed at Deuxponts, or Bipontium (Zweibrücken), in Bavaria.
BRIDEGROOM: A man newly married, or just about to be married.
BOOMDAS: A small African hyracoid mammal (Dendrohyrax arboreus) resembling the daman.

BRACHYCEPHALY: The state or condition of being brachycephalic; shortness of head.
BILOCULAR: Divided into two cells or compartments; as, a bilocular pericarp. Gray.
BY-BIDDER: One who bids at an auction in behalf of the auctioneer or owner, for the purpose of running up the price of articles. [U.S.]
BORDELLO: A brothel; a bawdyhouse; a house devoted to prostitution. [Obs.] B. Jonson.
BOSWELLIAN: Relating to, or characteristic of, Boswell, the biographer of Dr. Johnson.
BEDOTE: To cause to dote; to deceive. [Obs.] Chaucer.
BRIGAND: 1. A light-armed, irregular foot soldier. [Obs.] 2. A lawless fellow who lives by plunder; one of a band of robbers; especially, one of a gang living in mountain retreats; a highwayman; a freebooter. Giving them not a little the air of brigands or banditti. Jeffery.
BUBBLE SHELL: A marine univalve shell of the genus Bulla and allied genera, belonging to the Tectibranchiata.
BEWILDER: To lead into perplexity or confusion, as for want of a plain path; to perplex with mazes; or in general, to perplex or confuse greatly. Lost and bewildered in the fruitless search. Addison. Syn. -- To perplex; puzzle; entangle; confuse; confound; mystify; embarrass; lead astray.
BUTTER-SCOTCH: A kind of candy, mainly composed of sugar and butter. [Colloq.] Dickens.
BROCKEN SPECTER: A mountain specter (which see), esp. that observed on the Brocken, in the Harz Mountains.
BUOYANCY: 1. The property of floating on the surface of a liquid, or in a fluid, as in the atmosphere; specific lightness, which is inversely as the weight compared with that of an equal volume of water. 2. BERIBERI: An acute disease occurring in India, characterized by multiple inflammatory changes in the nerves, producing great muscular debility, a painful rigidity of the limbs, and cachexy.
BOOTTOPPING: 1. (Naut.) The act or process of daubing a vessel's bottom near the surface of the water with a mixture of tallow, sulphur, and resin, as a temporary protection against worms, after the slime, shells, etc., have been scraped off. 2. (Naut.) Sheathing a vessel with planking over felt.
BRYONY: The common name of several cucurbitaceous plants of the genus Bryonia. The root of B. alba (rough or white bryony) and of B. dioica is a strong, irritating cathartic. Black bryony, a plant (Tamus communis) so named from its dark glossy leaves and black root; black bindweed.
BICRESCENTIC: Having the form of a double crescent.
BUREAUCRATIST: An advocate for , or supporter of, bureaucracy.
BLOCKADER: 1. One who blockades. 2. (Naut.) A vessel employed in blockading.
BUDE BURNER: A burner consisting of two or more concentric Argand burners (the inner rising above the outer) and a central tube by which oxygen gas or common air is supplied.
BLEYME: An inflammation in the foot of a horse, between the sole and the bone. [Obs.]
BESEECHING: Entreating urgently; imploring; as, a beseeching look. -- Be*seech"ing*ly, adv. -- Be*seech"ing*ness, n.
BIPARTIBLE: Capable of being divided into two parts.
BROWNIST: A follower of Robert Brown, of England, in the 16th century, who taught that every church is complete and independent in itself when organized, and consists of members meeting in one place, having full power to elect and depose its officers. One who advocates the Brunonian system of medicine.
BY-PASSAGE: A passage different from the usual one; a byway.
BILLYCOCK: A round, low-crowned felt hat; a wideawake. "The undignified billycocks and pantaloons of the West." B. H. Chamberlain. Little acquiesced, and Ransome disguised him in a beard, and a loose set of clothes, and a billicock hat. Charles Reade.
BELLBIRD: (a) A South American bird of the genus Casmarhincos, and family Cotingidæ, of several species; the campanero. (b) The Myzantha melanophrys of Australia.

BARK BEETLE: A small beetle of many species (family Scolytidæ), which in the larval state bores under or in the bark of trees, often doing great damage.
BIGGIN: A child's cap; a hood, or something worn on the head. An old woman's biggin for a nightcap. Massinger. BRICKYARD: A place where bricks are made, especially an inclosed place.
BLOODSTONE: (a) A green siliceous stone sprinkled with red jasper, as if with blood; hence the name; -- called also heliotrope. (b) Hematite, an ore of iron yielding a blood red powder or "streak."
BED-MOLDING: The molding of a cornice immediately below the corona. Oxf. Gloss.
BLUSHFUL: Full of blushes. While from his ardent look the turning Spring Averts her blushful face. Thomson.
BLACKFISH: 1. (Zoöl.) A small kind of whale, of the genus Globicephalus, of several species. The most common is G. melas. Also sometimes applied to other whales of larger size. 2. (Zoöl.) BROADAX: 1. An ancient military weapon; a battle-ax. 2. An ax with a broad edge, for hewing timber.
BROUDED: Braided; broidered. [Obs.] Alle his clothes brouded up and down. Chaucer.
BOND: A relationship between people or groups based on shared feelings or experiences; a financial security.
BRAN: Pieces of cereal grain husks separated from flour after milling.
BUTTONWEED: The name of several plants of the genera Spermacoce and Diodia, of the Madder family.
BEAMY: 1. Emitting beams of light; radiant; shining. "Beamy gold." Tickell. 2. Resembling a beam in size and weight; massy. His double-biting ax, and beamy spear. Dryden. 3. Having horns, or antlers. Beamy stags in toils engage. Dryden.
BIBULOUSLY: In a bibulous manner; with profuse imbibition or absorption. De Quincey.
BRIDGEPOT: The adjustable socket, or step, of a millstone spindle. Knight.
BALLAHOO: A fast-sailing schooner, used in the Bermudas and West Indies.
BARBETTE: A mound of earth or a platform in a fortification, on which guns are mounted to fire over the parapet. En barbette, In barbette, said of guns when they are elevated so as to fire over the top of a parapet, and not through embrasures. -- Barbette gun, or Barbette battery, a single gun, or a number of guns, mounted in barbette, or partially protec...
BID: Offer a certain price for something, especially at an auction.
BICENTENNIAL: 1. Consisting of two hundred years. 2. Occurring every two hundred years. The two hundredth year or anniversary, or its celebration.
BY-ROOM: A private room or apartment. "Stand in some by-room" Shak.
BIRD-WITTED: Flighty; passing rapidly from one subject to another; not having the faculty of attention. Bacon.
BROTH: Soup consisting of meat or vegetable chunks cooked in stock, sometimes with rice or barley.
BACULINE: Of or pertaining to the rod or punishment with the rod.
BITTERROOT: A plant (Lewisia rediviva) allied to the purslane, but with fleshy, farinaceous roots, growing in the mountains of Idaho, Montana, etc. It gives the name to the Bitter Root mountains and river. The Indians call both the plant and the river Spæt'lum.
BINDING SCREW: A set screw used to bind parts together, esp. one for making a connection in an electrical circuit.
BRAHMINISM: The religion or system of doctrines of the Brahmans; the religion of Brahma.
BANNOCK: A kind of cake or bread, in shape flat and roundish, commonly made of oatmeal or barley meal and baked on an iron plate, or griddle; -- used in Scotland and the northern counties of England. Jamieson. Bannock fluke, the turbot. [Scot.]
BASS: The lowest adult male singing voice; a deep-toned musical instrument; an edible game fish.
BARRENNESS: The condition of being barren; sterility; unproductiveness. A total barrenness of invention. Dryden.
BESOTTED: Made sottish, senseless, or infatuated; characterized by drunken stupidity, or by infatuation; stupefied. "Besotted devotion." Sir W. Scott. -- Be*sot"ted*ly, adv. -- Be*sot"ted*ness, n. Milton.
BETON: The French name for concrete; hence, concrete made after the French fashion.
BARRY: , Divided into bars; -- said of the field.
BLOND: Of a fair color; light-colored; as, blond hair; a blond complexion.
BASKETFUL: As much as a basket will contain.
BAROTHERMOGRAPH: An instrument for recording both pressure and temperature, as of the atmosphere.
BEHOOF: Advantage; profit; benefit; interest; use. No mean recompense it brings To your behoof. Milton.
BLACKLY: In a black manner; darkly, in color; gloomily; threateningly; atrociously. "Deeds so blackly grim and horrid." Feltham.
BLEE: Complexion; color; hue; likeness; form. [Archaic] For him which is so bright of blee. Lament. of Mary Magd. That boy has a strong blee of his father. Forby.
BARRAMUNDI: (a) A remarkable Australian fresh-water ganoid fish of the genus Ceratodus. (b) An Australian river fish (Osteoglossum Leichhardtii).
BESPREAD: To spread or cover over. The carpet which bespread His rich pavilion's floor. Glover.
BUSCON: One who searches for ores; a prospector. [U.S.]

BAREFOOT: With the feet bare; without shoes or stockings.
BETWIXT: 1. In the space which separates; between. From betwixt two aged oaks. Milton. 2. From one to another of; mutually affecting. There was some speech of marriage Betwixt myself and her. Shak. Betwixt and between, in a midway position; so-so; neither one thing nor the other. [Colloq.]

BOATAGE: Conveyance by boat; also, a charge for such conveyance.
BYROAD: A private or obscure road. "Through slippery byroads" Swift.
BROWNNESS: The quality or state of being brown. Now like I brown (O lovely brown thy hair); Only in brownness beauty dwelleth there. Drayton.
BROIDER: To embroider. [Archaic] They shall make a broidered coat. Ex. xxviii. 4.

BIRTHLESS: Of mean extraction. [R.] Sir W. Scott.
BEST: Of the most excellent, effective, or desirable type or quality.

BOLT: A metal pin or bar used with a nut to fasten things together; a flash of lightning.
BASE-BURNER: A furnace or stove in which the fuel is contained in a hopper or chamber, and is fed to the fire as the lower stratum is consumed.
BEWRAP: To wrap up; to cover. Fairfax.
BOSKINESS: Boscage; also, the state or quality of being bosky.

BURREL: A sort of pear, called also the red butter pear, from its smooth, delicious, soft pulp. Same as Borrel.
BERME: 1. (Fort.) A narrow shelf or path between the bottom of a parapet and the ditch. 2. (Engineering) A ledge at the bottom of a bank or cutting, to catch earth that may roll down the slope, or to strengthen the bank.

BRIDLER: One who bridles; one who restrains and governs, as with a bridle. Milton.
BRAYING: Making a harsh noise; blaring. "Braying trumpets." Shak.
BEBLOOD: To make bloody; to stain with blood. [Obs.] Sheldon.
BALISAUR: A badgerlike animal of India (Arcionyx collaris).
BIJOUTRY: Small articles of virtu, as jewelry, trinkets, etc.

BIPUPILLATE: Having an eyelike spot on the wing, with two dots within it of a different color, as in some butterflies.

BLUESTONE: 1. Blue vitriol. Dunglison. 2. A grayish blue building stone, as that commonly used in the eastern United States.

BRACHYPTERES: A group of birds, including auks, divers, and penguins.

BALISTRARIA: A narrow opening, often cruciform, through which arrows might be discharged.

BIRTHING: Anything added to raise the sides of a ship. Bailey.
BILLBEETLE: A weevil or curculio of various species, as the corn weevil. See Curculio.

BLUE-VEINED: Having blue veins or blue streaks.
BUXOM: Plump, especially with large breasts (of a woman).

BENDY: Divided into an even number of bends; -- said of a shield or its charge. Cussans.

BULLFLY: Any large fly troublesome to cattle, as the gadflies and breeze flies.

BONAPARTISM: The policy of Bonaparte or of the Bonapartes.
BENUMBED: Made torpid; numbed; stupefied; deadened; as, a benumbed body and mind. -- Be*numbed"ness, n.
BATTLE SHIP: An armor-plated man-of-war built of steel and heavily armed, generally having from ten thousand to fifteen thousand tons displacement, and intended to be fit to meet the heaviest ships in line of battle.
BEWITCHERY: The power of bewitching or fascinating; bewitchment; charm; fascination. There is a certain bewitchery or fascination in words. South.
BIBLIOTAPHIST: One who hides away books, as in a tomb. [R.] Crabb.
BANDMASTER: The conductor of a musical band.
BOLDO: A fragrant evergreen shrub of Chili (Peumus Boldus). The bark is used in tanning, the wood for making charcoal, the leaves in medicine, and the drupes are eaten.
BRAKEMAN: 1. (Railroads) A man in charge of a brake or brakes. 2. (Mining) The man in charge of the winding (or hoisting) engine for a mine.
BESTIR: To put into brisk or vigorous action; to move with life and vigor; -- usually with the reciprocal pronoun. You have so bestirred your valor. Shak. Rouse and bestir themselves ere well awake. Milton.
BEAU MONDE: The fashionable world; people of fashion and gayety. Prior.
BODHISAT: One who has reached the highest degree of saintship, so that in his next incarnation he will be a Buddha, or savior of the world. -- Bo"dhi*sat`ship, n.
BRANLIN: A young salmon or parr, in the stage in which it has transverse black bands, as if burned by a gridiron. A small red worm or larva, used as bait for small fresh-water fish; -- so called from its red color.
BARGAINER: One who makes a bargain; -- sometimes in the sense of bargainor.
BLOWER: 1. One who, or that which, blows. 2. (Mech.) A device for producing a current of air; as: (a) A metal plate temporarily placed before the upper part of a grate or open fire. (b) A machine for producing an artificial blast or current of air by pressure, as for increasing the draft of a furnace, ventilating a building or shaft, cleansing gram, etc...
BATHING: Act of taking a bath or baths. Bathing machine, a small room on wheels, to be driven into the water, for the convenience of bathers, who undress and dress therein.
BOND SERVANT: A slave; one who is bound to service without wages. If thy brother . . . be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bond servant: but as an hired servant. Lev. xxv. 39, 40.
BANANA: A perennial herbaceous plant of almost treelike size (Musa sapientum); also, its edible fruit. See Musa. Note: The banana has a soft, herbaceous stalk, with leaves of great length and breadth. The flowers grow in bunches, covered with a sheath of a green or purple color; the fruit is five or six inches long, and over an inch in diameter; the pul...
BERBER: A member of a race somewhat resembling the Arabs, but often classed as Hamitic, who were formerly the inhabitants of the whole of North Africa from the Mediterranean southward into the Sahara, and who still occupy a large part of that region; -- called also Kabyles. Also, the language spoken by this people.
BOUNDEN: 1. Bound; fastened by bonds. [Obs.] 2. Under obligation; bound by some favor rendered; obliged; beholden. This holy word, that teacheth us truly our bounden duty toward our Lord God in every point. Ridley. 3. Made obligatory; imposed as a duty; binding. I am much bounden to your majesty. Shak.
BASILICAN: Of, relating to, or resembling, a basilica; basilical. There can be no doubt that the first churches in Constantinople were in the basilican form. Milman.
BILOCATION: Double location; the state or power of being in two places at the same instant; -- a miraculous power attributed to some of the saints. Tylor.
BELAY: 1. To lay on or cover; to adorn. [Obs.] Jacket . . . belayed with silver lace. Spenser. 2. (Naut.) To make fast, as a rope, by taking several turns with it round a pin, cleat, or kevel. Totten. 3. To lie in wait for with a view to assault. Hence: to block up or obstruct. [Obs.] Dryden. Belay thee! Stop.
BEQUOTE: To quote constantly or with great frequency.
BOULEVERSEMENT: Complete overthrow; disorder; a turning upside down.
BOEOTIAN: Of or pertaining to Boeotia; hence, stupid; dull; obtuse. -- n. A native of Boeotia; also, one who is dull and ignorant.
BEWIG: To cover (the head) with a wig. Hawthorne.
BOUNCE: 1. To strike or thump, so as to rebound, or to make a sudden noise; a knock loudly. Another bounces as hard as he can knock. Swift. Against his bosom bounced his heaving heart. Dryden. 2. To leap or spring suddenly or unceremoniously; to bound; as, she bounced into the room. Out bounced the mastiff. Swift. Bounced off his arm+chair. Thackeray. 3...
BYSSINE: Made of silk; having a silky or flaxlike appearance. Coles.
BRASSY: 1. Of or pertaining to brass; having the nature, appearance, or hardness, of brass. 2. Impudent; impudently bold. [Colloq.]
BRICKLE: Brittle; easily broken. [Obs. or Prov.] Spenser. As stubborn steel excels the brickle glass. Turbervile.
BRYONIN: A bitter principle obtained from the root of the bryony (Bryonia alba and B. dioica). It is a white, or slightly colored, substance, and is emetic and cathartic.
BISCOTIN: A confection made of flour, sugar, marmalade, and eggs; a sweet biscuit.
BRACHIOLARIA: (Zoöl.) A peculiar early larval stage of certain starfishes, having a bilateral structure, and swimming by means of bands of vibrating cilia.
BRELOQUE: A seal or charm for a watch chain. "His chains and breloques." Thackeray.
BITTERING: A bitter compound used in adulterating beer; bittern.
BELLIC: Of or pertaining to war; warlike; martial. [Obs.] "Bellic Cæsar." Feltham.
BAB: Lit., gate; -- a title given to the founder of Babism, and taken from that of Bab-ud-Din, assumed by him.
BIPECTINATED: Having two margins toothed like a comb.
BESCRIBBLE: To scribble over. "Bescribbled with impertinences." Milton.
BURNISHER: 1. One who burnishes. 2. A tool with a hard, smooth, rounded end or surface, as of steel, ivory, or agate, used in smoothing or polishing by rubbing. It has a variety of forms adapted to special uses.
BALE: A large wrapped or bound bundle of paper, hay, or cotton.
BABEL: A confused noise made by a number of voices; biblical tower of linguistic confusion.
BIPLANE: An aëroplane with two main supporting surfaces one above the other. Having, or consisting of, two superposed planes, aërocurves, or the like; of or pertaining to a biplane; as, a biplane rudder.
BUNCHBERRY: The dwarf cornel (Cornus Canadensis), which bears a dense cluster of bright red, edible berries.
BALDRIB: A piece of pork cut lower down than the sparerib, and destitute of fat. [Eng.] Southey.
BIRLAW: A law made by husbandmen respecting rural affairs; a rustic or local law or by-law. [Written also byrlaw, birlie, birley.]
BLUFFNESS: The quality or state of being bluff.
BOXEN: Made of boxwood; pertaining to, or resembling, the box (Buxus). [R.] The faded hue of sapless boxen leaves. Dryden.
BEWILDERMENT: 1. The state of being bewildered. 2. A bewildering tangle or confusion. He . . . soon lost all traces of it amid bewilderment of tree trunks and underbrush. Hawthorne.
BULL-NECKED: Having a short and thick neck like that of a bull. Sir W. Scott.
BAWL: 1. To cry out with a loud, full sound; to cry with vehemence, as in calling or exultation; to shout; to vociferate. 2. To cry loudly, as a child from pain or vexation. To proclaim with a loud voice, or by outcry, as a hawker or town-crier does. Swift. A loud, prolonged cry; an outcry.
BUTTERWEIGHT: Over weight. Swift. Note: Formerly it was a custom to give 18 ounces of butter for a pound.
BEGGARHOOD: The condition of being a beggar; also, the class of beggars.
BLOODSUCKER: 1. (Zoöl.) Any animal that sucks blood; esp., the leech (Hirudo medicinalis), and related species. 2. One who sheds blood; a cruel, bloodthirsty man; one guilty of bloodshed; a murderer. [Obs.] Shak. 3. A hard and exacting master, landlord, or money lender; an extortioner.
BRACHYCERAL: Having short antennæ, as certain insects.
BOWLER: One who plays at bowls, or who rolls the ball in cricket or any other game.
BYRONIC: Pertaining to, or in the style of, Lord Byron. With despair and Byronic misanthropy. Thackeray
BROMYRITE: Silver bromide, a rare mineral; -- called also bromargyrite.
BRODEKIN: A buskin or half-boot. [Written also brodequin.] [Obs.]
BANCO: A bank, especially that of Venice. Note: This term is used in some parts of Europe to indicate bank money, as distinguished from the current money, when this last has become depreciated.
BABBLE: 1. To utter words indistinctly or unintelligibly; to utter inarticulate sounds; as a child babbles. 2. To talk incoherently; to utter unmeaning words. 3. To talk much; to chatter; to prate. 4. To make a continuous murmuring noise, as shallow water running over stones. In every babbling he finds a friend. Wordsworth. Note: Hounds are said to babb...
BUNTINE: A thin woolen stuff, used chiefly for flags, colors, and ships' signals.
BIAS: 1. A weight on the side of the ball used in the game of bowls, or a tendency imparted to the ball, which turns it from a straight line. Being ignorant that there is a concealed bias within the spheroid, which will . . . swerve away. Sir W. Scott. 2. A learning of the mind; propensity or prepossession toward an object or view, not leaving the min...
BOUTEFEU: An incendiary; an inciter of quarrels. [Obs.] Animated by . . . John à Chamber, a very boutefeu, . . . they entered into open rebellion. Bacon.
BULLOCK: 1. A young bull, or any male of the ox kind. Take thy father's young bullock, even the second bullock of seven years old. Judges vi. 25. 2. An ox, steer, or stag. To bully. [Obs.] She shan't think to bullock and domineer over me. Foote. BULLOCK'S-EYE Bul"lock's-eye`, n. See Bull's-eye, 3.
BULLFICE: A kind of fungus. See Puffball.
BARKEEPER: One who keeps or tends a bar for the sale of liquors.
BIELD: A shelter. Same as Beild. [Scot.] To shelter. [Scot.]
BATOIDEI: The division of fishes which includes the rays and skates.
BEARDLESSNESS: The state or quality of being destitute of beard.
BACON: Cured meat from the back or sides of a pig.
BETHABARA WOOD: A highly elastic wood, used for fishing rods, etc. The tree is unknown, but it is thought to be East Indian.
BAPTISM: The act of baptizing; the application of water to a person, as a sacrament or religious ceremony, by which he is initiated into the visible church of Christ. This is performed by immersion, sprinkling, or pouring.
BATHYMETRICAL: Pertaining to bathymetry; relating to the measurement of depths, especially of depths in the sea.
BARPOST: A post sunk in the ground to receive the bars closing a passage into a field.
BRIC-A BRAC: Miscellaneous curiosities and works of decorative art, considered collectively. A piece of bric-a-brac, any curious or antique article of virtu, as a piece of antiquated furniture or metal work, or an odd knickknack.
BASCINET: A light helmet, at first open, but later made with a visor. [Written also basinet, bassinet, basnet.]
BEGUILEMENT: The act of beguiling, or the state of being beguiled.
BETHINK: To call to mind; to recall or bring to recollection, reflection, or consideration; to think; to consider; -- generally followed by a reflexive pronoun, often with of or that before the subject of thought. I have bethought me of another fault. Shak. The rest . . . may . . . bethink themselves, and recover. Milton. We bethink a means to break it o...
BARBIZON SCHOOL: A French school of the middle of the 19th century centering in the village of Barbizon near the forest of Fontainebleau. Its members went straight to nature in disregard of academic tradition, treating their subjects faithfully and with poetic feeling for color, light, and atmosphere. It is exemplified, esp. in landscapes, by Corot, Rousseau, Da...
BATISTE: Originally, cambric or lawn of fine linen; now applied also to cloth of similar texture made of cotton.
BRUSSELS: A city of Belgium, giving its name to a kind of carpet, a kind of lace, etc. Brussels carpet, a kind of carpet made of worsted yarn fixed in a foundation web of strong linen thread. BY-LANE: A private lane, or one opening out of the usual road.
BAAL: 1. (Myth.) The supreme male divinity of the Phoenician and Canaanitish nations. Note: The name of this god occurs in the Old Testament and elsewhere with qualifying epithets subjoined, answering to the different ideas of his character; as, Baal-berith (the Covenant Baal), Baal-zebub (Baal of the fly). 2. pl. The whole class of divinities to whom...
BOTRYOIDAL: Having the form of a bunch of grapes; like a cluster of grapes, as a mineral presenting an aggregation of small spherical or spheroidal prominences.
BUREAU: 1. Originally, a desk or writing table with drawers for papers. Swift. 2. The place where such a bureau is used; an office where business requiring writing is transacted. 3. Hence: A department of public business requiring a force of clerks; the body of officials in a department who labor under the direction of a chief. Note: On the continent of...
BAILOR: One who delivers goods or money to another in trust.
BREECH SIGHT: A device attached to the breech of a firearm, to guide the eye, in conjunction with the front sight, in taking aim.
BIDENT: An instrument or weapon with two prongs.
BLOODINESS: 1. The state of being bloody. 2. Disposition to shed blood; bloodthirstiness. All that bloodiness and savage cruelty which was in our nature. Holland.
BURRING MACHINE: A machine for cleansing wool of burs, seeds, and other substances.
BEARISH: Partaking of the qualities of a bear; resembling a bear in temper or manners. Harris.
BELOWT: To treat as a lout; to talk abusively to. [Obs.] Camden.
BEGEM: To adorn with gems, or as with gems. Begemmed with dewdrops. Sir W. Scott. Those lonely realms bright garden isles begem. Shelley.
BRAVO: Used to express approval when a performer or other person has done something well.
BECALM: 1. To render calm or quiet; to calm; to still; to appease. Soft whispering airs . . . becalm the mind. Philips. 2. To keep from motion, or stop the progress of, by the stilling of the wind; as, the fleet was becalmed.
BODLEIAN: Of or pertaining to Sir Thomas Bodley, or to the celebrated library at Oxford, founded by him in the sixteenth century.
BANCAL: An ornamental covering, as of carpet or leather, for a bench or form.
BICOLLIGATE: Having the anterior toes connected by a basal web.
BOTRYOSE: (a) Having the form of a cluster of grapes. (b) Of the racemose or acropetal type of inflorescence. Gray.
BLACKPOLL: A warbler of the United States (Dendroica striata).
BADIAN: An evergreen Chinese shrub of the Magnolia family (Illicium anisatum), and its aromatic seeds; Chinese anise; star anise.
BUHRSTONE: A cellular, flinty rock, used for mill stones. [Written also burrstone.]
BIS-: A form of Bi-, sometimes used before s, c, or a vowel.
BULIMIA: A disease in which there is a perpetual and insatiable appetite for food; a diseased and voracious appetite.
BUSHIDO: The unwritten code of moral principles regulating the actions of the Japanese knighthood, or Samurai; the chivalry of Japan. Unformulated, Bushido was and still is the animating spirit, the motor force of our country. Inazo Nitobé.
BELGRAVIAN: Belonging to Belgravia (a fashionable quarter of London, around Pimlico), or to fashionable life; aristocratic.
BRACHYGRAPHER: A writer in short hand; a stenographer. He asked the brachygrapher whether he wrote the notes of the sermon. Gayton.
BRYOZOAN: Of or pertaining to the Bryozoa. -- n. One of the Bryozoa.
BODILY: 1. Having a body or material form; physical; corporeal; consisting of matter. You are a mere spirit, and have no knowledge of the bodily part of us. Tatler. 2. Of or pertaining to the body, in distinction from the mind. "Bodily defects." L'Estrange. 3. Real; actual; put in execution. [Obs.] Be brought to bodily act. Shak. Bodily fear, apprehensi...
BROW: A person's forehead; the ridge over the eye.
BEDDED: Provided with a bed; as, double-bedded room; placed or arranged in a bed or beds.
BOBBY: Informal British term for a police officer.
BEWITCHMENT: 1. The act of bewitching, or the state of being bewitched. Tylor. 2. The power of bewitching or charming. Shak.
BACKSWORD: 1. A sword with one sharp edge. 2. In England, a stick with a basket handle, used in rustic amusements; also, the game in which the stick is used. Also called singlestick. Halliwell.
BLASTOIDEA: One of the divisions of Crinoidea found fossil in paleozoic rocks; pentremites. They are so named on account of their budlike form.
BONNINESS: The quality of being bonny; gayety [R.]
BORDER: 1. The outer part or edge of anything, as of a garment, a garden, etc.; margin; verge; brink. Upon the borders of these solitudes. Bentham. In the borders of death. Barrow. 2. BRIDE: A woman on her wedding day or just before or after the event.
BANDLET: A small band or fillet; any little band or flat molding, compassing a column, like a ring. Gwilt. Same as Bandelet.
BITTERNESS: 1. The quality or state of being bitter, sharp, or acrid, in either a literal or figurative sense; implacableness; resentfulness; severity; keenness of reproach or sarcasm; deep distress, grief, or vexation of mind. BODICE: 1. A kind of under waist stiffened with whalebone, etc., worn esp. by women; a corset; stays. 2. A close-fitting outer waist or vest forming the upper part of a woman's dress, or a portion of it. Her bodice half way she unlaced. Prior.
BYSSUS: 1. A cloth of exceedingly fine texture, used by the ancients. It is disputed whether it was of cotton, linen, or silk. [Written also byss and byssin.] 2. (Zoöl.) A tuft of long, tough filaments which are formed in a groove of the foot, and issue from between the valves of certain bivalve mollusks, as the Pinna and Mytilus, by which they attach t...
BONFIRE: A large fire built in the open air, as an expression of public joy and exultation, or for amusement. Full soon by bonfire and by bell, We learnt our liege was passing well. Gay.
BOXHAULING: A method of going from one tack to another. See Boxhaul.
BUM: A vagrant; a person who devotes their life to a specified activity (e.g. beach bum).
BIDDY: A woman, especially an elderly one regarded as annoying or gossipy.
BY-CORNER: A private corner. Britain being a by-corner, out of the road of the world. Fuller.
BONDAR: A small quadruped of Bengal (Paradoxurus bondar), allied to the genet; -- called also musk cat.
BARROW: 1. A support having handles, and with or without a wheel, on which heavy or bulky things can be transported by hand. See Handbarrow, and Wheelbarrow. 2. BESTIARY: A treatise on beasts; esp., one of the moralizing or allegorical beast tales written in the Middle Ages. A bestiary . . . in itself one of the numerous mediæval renderings of the fantastic mystical zoölogy. Saintsbury.
BIGENTIAL: Including two tribes or races of men.
BOTANIZE: To seek after plants for botanical investigation; to study plants. To explore for botanical purposes.
BORNEOL: A rare variety of camphor, C10H17.OH, resembling ordinary camphor, from which it can be produced by reduction. It is said to occur in the camphor tree of Borneo and Sumatra (Dryobalanops camphora), but the natural borneol is rarely found in European or American commerce, being in great request by the Chinese. BLACKBAND: An earthy carbonate of iron containing considerable carbonaceous matter; -- valuable as an iron ore.
BARTLETT: A Bartlett pear, a favorite kind of pear, which originated in England about 1770, and was called Williams' Bonchrétien. It was brought to America, and distributed by Mr. Enoch Bartlett, of Dorchester, Massachusetts.
BOWER-BARFF PROCESS: A certain process for producing upon articles of iron or steel an adherent coating of the magnetic oxide of iron (which is not liable to corrosion by air, moisture, or ordinary acids). BURNT: Destroyed or damaged by fire or heat.
BENEDICTION: 1. The act of blessing. 2. A blessing; an expression of blessing, prayer, or kind wishes in favor of any person or thing; a solemn or affectionate invocation of happiness. So saying, he arose; whom Adam thus Followed with benediction. Milton. Homeward serenely she walked with God's benediction upon her. Longfellow. Specifically: The short prayer...
BUTTONS: A boy servant, or page, -- in allusion to the buttons on his livry. [Colloq.] Dickens.
BUSKINED: 1. Wearing buskins. Her buskined virgins traced the dewy lawn. Pope. 2. Trodden by buskins; pertaining to tragedy. "The buskined stage." Milton.
BATTAILANT: Prepared for battle; combatant; warlike. Spenser. -- n. A combatant. Shelton.
BRACHYPTERA: A group of Coleoptera having short wings; the rove beetles.
BIBBE: To drink; to tipple. [Obs.] This miller hath . . . bibbed ale. Chaucer.
BARNACLE: Any cirriped crustacean adhering to rocks, floating timber, ships, etc., esp. BOWSTRING: 1. The string of a bow. 2. A string used by the Turks for strangling offenders. Bowstring bridge, a bridge formed of an arch of timber or iron, often braced, the thrust of which is resisted by a tie forming a chord of the arch. -- Bowstring girder, an arched beam strengthened by a tie connecting its two ends. -- Bowstring hemp (Bot.), the tenaci...
BARBELLATE: Having short, stiff hairs, often barbed at the point. Gray.
BARBARIC: 1. Of, or from, barbarian nations; foreign; -- often with reference to barbarous nations of east. "Barbaric pearl and gold." Milton. 2. Of or pertaining to, or resembling, an uncivilized person or people; barbarous; barbarian; destitute of refinement. "Wild, barbaric music." Sir W. Scott.
BAT PRINTING: A mode of printing on glazed ware.
BOSHBOK: A kind of antelope. See Bush buck.
BUBALINE: Resembling a buffalo. Bubaline antelope (Zoöl.), the bubale.
BATTLER: A student at Oxford who is supplied with provisions from the buttery; formerly, one who paid for nothing but what he called for, answering nearly to a sizar at Cambridge. Wright.
BOSPORIAN: Of or pertaining to the Thracian or the Cimmerian Bosporus. The Alans forced the Bosporian kings to pay them tribute and exterminated the Taurians. Tooke.
BOULEVARDIER: A frequenter of a city boulevard, esp. in Paris. F. Harrison.
BOOKSTALL: A stall or stand where books are sold.
BAILER: See Bailor. 1. One who bails or lades. 2. A utensil, as a bucket or cup, used in bailing; a machine for bailing water out of a pit.
BATTING: 1. The act of one who bats; the management of a bat in playing games of ball. Mason. 2. Cotton in sheets, prepared for use in making quilts, etc.; as, cotton batting.
BOROSILICATE: A double salt of boric and silicic acids, as in the natural minerals tourmaline, datolite, etc.
BRUTENESS: 1. Brutality. [Obs.] Spenser. 2. Insensibility. "The bruteness of nature." Emerson.
BRUTIFY: To make like a brute; to make senseless, stupid, or unfeeling; to brutalize. Any man not quite brutified and void of sense. Barrow.

BACKWARDATION: The seller's postponement of delivery of stock or shares, with the consent of the buyer, upon payment of a premium to the latter; -- also, the premium so paid. See Contango. Biddle.
BENT GRASS: Same as Bent, a kind of grass.
BODHISATTWA: One who has reached the highest degree of saintship, so that in his next incarnation he will be a Buddha, or savior of the world. -- Bo"dhi*sat`ship, n.
BIROSTRATE: Having a double beak, or two processes resembling beaks. The capsule is bilocular and birostrated. Ed. Encyc.
BEARWARD: A keeper of bears. See Bearherd. [R.] Shak.

BLOODLETTING: The act or process of letting blood or bleeding, as by opening a vein or artery, or by cupping or leeches; -- esp. applied to venesection.
BAREHEADED: Having the head uncovered; as, a bareheaded girl.
BADIGEON: A cement or paste (as of plaster and freestone, or of sawdust and glue or lime) used by sculptors, builders, and workers in wood or stone, to fill holes, cover defects, or finish a surface.
BROMLIFE: A carbonate of baryta and lime, intermediate between witherite and strontianite; -- called also alstonite.
BIRK: A birch tree. [Prov. Eng.] "The silver birk." Tennyson. A small European minnow (Leuciscus phoxinus).
BALNEOTHERAPY: The treatment of disease by baths.
BOUD: A weevil; a worm that breeds in malt, biscuit, etc. [Obs.] Tusser., n. BURHEL: The wild Himalayan, or blue, sheep (Ovis burrhel).

BABY FARMER: One who keeps a baby farm.
BIMUSCULAR: Having two adductor muscles, as a bivalve mollusk.
BARONAGE: 1. The whole body of barons or peers. The baronage of the kingdom. Bp. Burnet. 2. The dignity or rank of a baron. 3. The land which gives title to a baron. [Obs.]
BITTOCK: A small bit of anything, of indefinite size or quantity; a short distance. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott.
BASELY: 1. In a base manner; with despicable meanness; dishonorably; shamefully. 2. Illegitimately; in bastardy. [Archaic] Knolles.
BENISON: Blessing; beatitude; benediction. Shak. More precious than the benison of friends. Talfourd.
